nodes.name: Webhook: Recipe Generation Request
nodes.notes: POST /generate-recipe, the entry point for the Angular app. Response mode is 'Using Respond to Webhook Node', so every branch sets its own status code instead of answering automatically.

nodes.name: Extract Client IP
nodes.notes: Reads the caller's IP from $json.ip, falling back to the x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip and cf-connecting-ip headers, and checks its shape. Deletes the raw headers from the item right away so the address travels no further through the run than it has to.

nodes.name: IP Valid?
nodes.notes: Without a usable IP the quota cannot be keyed, so the request is turned away rather than let through unmetered.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { error: "invalid_request", message: "Could not determine a valid client IP address for this request." } }}

nodes.name: Respond: 400 Invalid IP
nodes.notes: 400 with { error: 'invalid_request' }, the error shape recipe-generator.service.ts expects.

nodes.name: Validate Request Payload
nodes.notes: Re-checks ingredients, servings, helpers and the enum fields against the same ranges the Angular form enforces, including the per-unit quantity cap (min 1, max 2000 g / 2000 ml / 20 pieces). Defence in depth: the webhook is public and anyone can post to it. Amounts over the cap are clamped, broken ones are a 400.

nodes.name: Payload Valid?
nodes.notes: Splits into the 400 branch or into the Firestore chain.

nodes.name: Respond: 400 Invalid Request
nodes.notes: 400 listing the collected payloadErrors, so the client can say what was wrong instead of showing a generic failure.

nodes.name: Set Quota IP Salt
nodes.notes: Holds quotaIpSalt, the only secret left in this workflow - the Firebase service account now lives in the n8n credential "Firestore Service Account" (Google Service Account API). The salt has to match the one in the Recipe Quota Status workflow character for character, otherwise this workflow counts up a different document than the status endpoint reads. 'Include Other Fields' is on so the value travels with the item.

nodes.name: Compute Quota Keys
nodes.notes: Builds the daily document ids: quota_ip/<date>_<salted SHA-256 of the IP> and quota_total/<date>, then drops clientIp. No raw address is ever written to Firestore. The date is UTC, so the limit resets at midnight UTC, not local midnight.

nodes.name: Reserve Quota Slot
nodes.notes: One atomic Firestore :commit that raises both counters by 1 with an increment transform. Authenticates with the "Firestore Service Account" credential (Google Service Account API, scope .../auth/datastore), which signs the JWT and sets the Bearer header itself. updateMask ['date'] leaves count alone, which lets the same call create the document on the first request of the day.

nodes.name: Parse Quota Reservation
nodes.notes: Reads the post-increment counts out of writeResults[].transformResults. These values are authoritative: overlapping requests get 3 and 4 instead of both getting 3.

nodes.name: Check Quota Limits
nodes.notes: ipCount > 3 or totalCount > 12. The counts already include this request, so the limit trips one step later than it would with a read-first gate.

nodes.name: Release Quota Slot
nodes.notes: The same commit with increment -1, same credential. The slot was taken before the limit was known, so a rejected request hands it back before the 429 goes out.

nodes.name: Build Quota Exceeded Response
nodes.notes: Picks the message by which limit tripped - the caller's own three or the twelve shared across all users - and reports the counts as they stand after the release.

nodes.name: Respond: 429 Quota Exceeded
nodes.notes: 429 with error 'quota_exceeded'. The Angular loading view turns this into the 'Daily limit reached' notice instead of a generic error.

nodes.name: Build LLM Request
nodes.notes: Builds only the user message for the chain (servings, cooks, cuisine, diet rule, time hint, ingredients). The JSON schema moved into the Recipe Output Parser sub-node and the model into the OpenAI Chat Model sub-node.

messageValues.message:
You are the recipe generator of the app Code a Cuisine.
You write practical home-cooking recipes in English.
Rules:
- Return exactly three clearly different recipes for the same request.
- Build them around the ingredients the user already has; use as many of them as sensible.
- Anything else the dish needs goes into missingIngredients, at most three common staples.
- Keep to the requested cuisine, diet, servings and cooking time.
- Spread the steps over the given number of cooks; with a single cook every step is assignedTo 1 and isParallel is false.
- Nutrition is per serving and has to fit the ingredients: calories must roughly match protein times 4 plus carbs times 4 plus fat times 9.
- Plain text only, no markdown, no emoji.

nodes.name: OpenAI: Generate Recipes
nodes.notes: Basic LLM Chain (checklist item 13): the model comes in through the OpenAI Chat Model sub-node, the answer's shape through the Recipe Output Parser sub-node, and the prompt rules sit in the system message. On an error - timeout, rate limit, outage, or an answer the parser cannot validate - the run leaves through the second output and the fallback node answers instead.

nodes.name: OpenAI Chat Model
nodes.notes: The OpenAI credential stored in n8n; the API key is never part of this file. The model id is the one the old "Build LLM Request" Code node carried as its MODEL constant - change it here now.

nodes.name: Recipe Output Parser
nodes.notes: The same JSON schema the old HTTP request pinned with response_format.json_schema, so the contract with the Angular frontend is unchanged. The parser hands its data back under an "output" key, which "Validate & Normalise Recipes" unwraps.

nodes.name: Validate & Normalise Recipes
nodes.notes: Unwraps the output parser's result ({ output: { recipes: [...] } }), repairs what the model may still get wrong and enforces the caps from firestore.rules. Throws when the answer is unusable, which routes the run to the fallback node.

nodes.name: Generate Fallback Recipes
nodes.notes: The former mock generator, now the safety net: it runs when the OpenAI call fails or its answer cannot be validated, so the app always gets three recipes. Same output shape as the real path.

nodes.name: Respond: 200 Success
nodes.notes: 200 with { recipes, quota: { ipRemaining, totalRemaining } }, exactly the GenerateResponse shape the Angular service reads.
